title: Micro-slice streaming observability, span sampling and redaction shim
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Implement a micro-slice observability layer for streamed model outputs that produces per-slice metrics, attached trace spans with controlled sampling, and an inline redaction/pseudonymization pass that operates on streamed tokens. The work also introduces a compatibility shim to normalize OpenAI-style delta streaming and function-call events into Redwood's telemetry model so downstream dashboards and rollouts can reason about slices uniformly.
rationale: Current streaming telemetry emits coarse 'request-level' metrics and unstructured logs, which hides transient failures, mid-stream latency spikes, and PII leakage risk inside long responses. Teams shipping streaming tool-calls and structured outputs lack consistent traces and per-chunk histograms to debug latency regressions and cost anomalies. This ticket reduces blast radius of PII in logs, improves signal for the console, and standardizes compatibility across client SDKs.
implementation_plan: 1) Introduce 'micro-slice' concept: break a stream into ordered slices (heartbeat markers every N tokens or on function-call boundaries). 2) Emit a slice-level metric bundle (latency_ms, tokens_emitted, error_flag, byte_size). 3) Create a tracing span per slice with a lightweight deterministic ID; attach span references to request-level trace. 4) Implement a sampling policy that keeps all spans for first 3 slices, then samples 1/N for subsequent slices (configurable per-customer). 5) Add an in-path redaction stage that runs on emitted tokens: pattern-based PII scrubbing + configurable pseudonymization hooks. 6) Build a compatibility shim that converts OpenAI delta events (content, role, function_call.start/arg/chunk) into normalized slice events with consistent metric tags. 7) Wire metrics into console routes and add slice histograms to per-route dashboards. 8) Add e2e tests and a developer doc for SDK authors.
acceptance_criteria: Slice-level metrics emitted for all streaming responses: latency_ms, tokens_emitted, error_flag, bytes
Trace spans created for slices and linkable to request-level trace IDs in distributed tracing backends
Sampling policy is configurable via customer settings and defaults reduce cardinality by >75% without losing first-slice fidelity
Redaction stage removes or pseudonymizes tokens matching PII patterns in streamed logs and prevents PII from being written to the live logging pipeline
Compatibility shim successfully normalizes OpenAI-style delta streams from SDK tests into our slice model and preserves function-call boundaries
Console shows per-route slice histograms and additive token counters for a test workload
Automated tests validating redaction behavior for a set of canonical PII inputs exist and run in CI
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created. Initial scoping with PM and runtime team. Identified existing telemetry hooks and proposed micro-slice interface.

2025-02-18: Design sync — agreed on heartbeat marker every 64 tokens and explicit slice boundary on function-call start/finish. Decided to use deterministic span IDs derived from request-id + slice-index.

2025-02-22: Spike complete — micro-slice metrics prove low overhead (sample app + local gpu harness). Prototype redaction library (pattern engine) implemented in Rust core, exposes FFI for runtime path.

2025-02-26: Security review kickoff scheduled. Early findings: regex-based scrubbing insufficient for some structured PII in code blocks; added pseudonymization hook for customer-managed transformations.
2025-03-03: PR opened for slice metrics and span plumbing (RFC: streaming-slice-telemetry). Compatibility shim tests added for OpenAI delta events. Awaiting code review from infra and console owners.
qa_steps: Run SDK smoke test that streams a 5k-token generated response and verify slice metrics appear in test Grafana
Inject PII testcases from drive spreadsheet and ensure no PII written to log ingestion (check S3 partition)
Run distributed tracing heatmap and verify first-three-slice spans always present and subsequent spans sampled per policy
Validate OpenAI delta compatibility by replaying recorded client events and asserting normalized slice events
risks: High-cardinality trace emission if sampling misconfigured — mitigated by default aggressive sampling and rate limits
Edge-case redaction in code blocks could alter developer-visible outputs if transformations are aggressive; we surface pseudonymization flag to end-users
Compatibility shim may not cover non-OpenAI streaming variants from third-party SDKs — plan to iterate with SDK owners
notes: Proposal favors deterministic span IDs to ease correlation for customer support. We must ensure redaction is asynchronous with logging backpressure to avoid added tail latency. Consider moving heavy NLP PII detectors to an offline job for long responses.
